title: Complete Yeast Protein Extraction
author: Tobias von der Haar
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.g8wbzxe
materials: Prepare the basic solutions: Extraction Buffer: 0.1 M NaOH, 0.05 M EDTA, 2% SDS (Note: before use, this buffer is supplemented with 2% 2-mercaptoethanol. With 2-ME the shelf life is several hours, without 2-ME the shelf life of this solution is ~ 1 week). Caution: This buffer is strongly alkaline and additional protective equipment (gloves and goggles) should be worn while preparing and handling it. Neutralisation Buffer: 4 M acetic acid in water. Neat acetic acid is 11 M in concentration. Loading buffer: 0.25 M Tris-HCl pH 6.8, 50% glycerol, 0.05% bromophenolblue.

steps.title: Harvest yeast cells
steps.instruction: Collect approximately 1 × 10⁸ logarithmically growing yeast cells (≈5 OD₆₀₀ units) by centrifuging in a microcentrifuge at maximum speed for 1 minute, then discard the supernatant completely.

steps.title: Pre‑heat heating block
steps.instruction: Set a heating block to 96 °C (extraction is efficient at ≥80 °C).

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer and lyse cells
steps.instruction: Freshly add 20 µL of 2‑mercaptoethanol to 1 mL of extraction buffer (scale proportionally for more than five extractions). Resuspend the pelleted yeast cells in 200 µL of this supplemented buffer, then incubate the suspension at 96 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Neutralize lysate
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of neutralization buffer to the heated suspension and vortex briefly to mix.

steps.title: Add loading buffer
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of SDS‑PAGE loading buffer to the neutralized lysate and vortex again to ensure thorough mixing.

steps.title: Prepare sample for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: The lysate is now ready for loading onto SDS‑PAGE gels. Optional: clear the extract by a brief centrifugation step (not required). Loading the uncleared, well‑resuspended cell slurry directly into the gel wells can improve extraction efficiency.
